In fact, the auth decorator's exception handling allows the unauthenticated request to reach the handler, so order data is exposed without authentication.
finding.evidence: GET /orders/1 with no Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and the seeded customer's order, including items, payment amount, and refunds. The route at shopapi/orders.py:46-49 uses get_order() rather than own_order().

reason: The finding identifies the IDOR in show_order, and also describes the fail-open authentication decorator that lets unauthenticated requests reach the route.

finding.title: JWT signing secret is hardcoded and permits forged staff tokens
finding.description: The HS256 signing key is committed in source. Anyone who obtains the source or its package can mint a token with a staff subject and role; admin authorization trusts the database role for that subject.
finding.evidence: Using the committed key hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d, a locally generated HS256 token with sub=3 was accepted by GET /admin/users and returned HTTP 200. Token verification and staff lookup are in shopapi/auth.py:23-45.

reason: The finding identifies the hardcoded JWT signing secret in config.py, which allows attackers to forge tokens.

finding.title: Refresh accepts tokens without verifying their signature
finding.description: The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with verify_signature=False and only checks that the subject exists. Any attacker who obtains or alters a token can obtain a new valid session token; expiry, role and all other claims are not authenticated at this step.
finding.evidence: shopapi/auth.py:96-107 explicitly disables signature verification and then calls make_token() for the decoded subject. The endpoint also accepts expired tokens by design, so there is no cryptographic proof that the refresh request was issued by the server.

reason: The refresh endpoint disables signature verification and issues a valid token for the decoded subject, allowing forged tokens to take over accounts.

finding.title: Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes
finding.description: hash_password uses a single fast unsalted SHA-256 digest. A database disclosure permits efficient offline cracking and makes identical passwords identifiable; an adaptive password hash such as Argon2id, scrypt, or bcrypt is required.
finding.evidence: shopapi/auth.py:15-20 hashes passwords directly with hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(), and registration/reset store that value at lines 77-78 and 158-159.

reason: The finding identifies unsalted, fast SHA-256 password storage in hash_password, matching V09.

finding.title: Payment webhook signature does not cover payment status or amount
finding.description: The signature is an HMAC of only order_id. Anyone able to submit a valid signature for an order can change status and amount_pence without invalidating it; the handler accepts the client-supplied amount and can mark an order paid for zero or an arbitrary amount.
finding.evidence: webhook_signature at shopapi/payments.py:53-55 signs only str(order_id), while payment_webhook at lines 69-71 trusts event.status and int(event.amount_pence). The signed message must include the complete canonical event, especially amount and status.

reason: The webhook signature covers only the order ID, allowing the status and amount to be changed without invalidating it.

finding.title: Payment-status timeout fails open and marks the order paid
finding.description: When the payment provider times out, the exception handler sets status to paid and transitions the order to processing with the full total. A provider outage or induced timeout therefore grants goods without a confirmed payment.
finding.evidence: shopapi/payments.py:37-45 catches requests.Timeout, assigns status='paid', and updates paid_pence=total_pence. The comment confirms this is the production timeout behavior.

reason: The finding identifies the payment-status timeout being treated as paid in confirm_payment, allowing orders to be processed without confirmed payment.

finding.title: Request logging records credentials and other sensitive POST bodies
finding.description: Every POST, PUT, and PATCH body is logged verbatim up to 2,000 characters. Login passwords, reset codes, bearer-like application data, payment data, and personal information can consequently be stored in application logs.
finding.evidence: shopapi/__init__.py:29-31 calls request.get_data(as_text=True) for every mutating request. /auth/login and /auth/reset/confirm accept passwords/codes in those bodies.

reason: It identifies log_request in shopapi/__init__.py recording sensitive request bodies, including passwords and reset codes.

finding.title: Password-reset codes are brute-forceable and rate limits are absent
finding.description: Reset codes are generated with non-cryptographic random.random() in an eight-digit space. Confirmation has no attempt counter, throttling, or lockout, so an attacker can make unlimited guesses during the 30-minute validity window.
finding.evidence: shopapi/auth.py:135 generates the code with random.random(); lines 143-161 compare it without tracking attempts or rate limiting. The request and confirmation endpoints are publicly callable.

reason: It identifies the predictable, brute-forceable password-reset codes generated with random.random() and lacking attempt limits.

finding.title: Attacker-controlled display names reach an admin SQL query
finding.description: A customer controls display_name through registration and account update. The admin review report interpolates that stored value into SQL, allowing a malicious customer to inject SQL when staff query the report for that customer.
finding.evidence: shopapi/admin.py:74-80 loads customer.display_name and inserts it into an f-string SQL WHERE clause. The attacker-controlled value is accepted by shopapi/auth.py:116-125 without escaping.

reason: The finding identifies second-order SQL injection in reviews_by_customer, where a customer-controlled display_name is interpolated into the admin report query.

finding.title: The application is launched with Flask debug mode enabled
finding.description: The production entry point calls app.run(debug=True). If this entry point is used outside a tightly controlled development environment, unhandled exceptions expose the interactive debugger and detailed diagnostics, and the reloader/debug server is not suitable for production.
finding.evidence: run.py:5-6 unconditionally invokes app.run(host='127.0.0.1', port=5000, debug=True).

reason: It identifies run.py enabling Flask debug mode, matching V04.

finding.title: Checkout never checks or decrements product stock
finding.description: Checkout creates an order from the basket without checking current stock and never updates products.stock. Repeated or concurrent checkouts can sell unlimited units of a product whose catalogue stock is zero or low.
finding.evidence: shopapi/basket.py:61-74 inserts the order and items using basket_json prices, but contains no stock predicate, reservation, or stock update.

reason: Checkout’s failure to validate or decrement stock is a distinct real business-logic flaw not listed in the answer key.
